slots.purpose: Debate has very few written rules, so the two teams argue about the rest of the rules in the round.
slots.subject: A square game board where only the near part has its grid drawn. The squares stop part way across, and the far part of the board is plain and blank. One round game piece stands on the drawn squares at the left, and one stands on the drawn squares at the right, facing each other.
slots.composition: Seen from slightly above and in front, so the board reads as a square. The drawn grid covers about the front third of the board; the rest of the board is empty. The two pieces stand near the front edge, one left and one right, with clear space between them. Nothing else is in the picture.
slots.colors: The board is white with a black outline; the drawn squares alternate white and light grey #e1e4e8. The left piece is aff blue #0055b8. The right piece is neg red #f2232d. Both pieces have black outlines and are the same size and shape.
slots.avoid: No dice, cards, letters, numbers or symbols on the board. No hands or people. Do not show either piece moving or knocking the other over.
slots.alt: A game board with only some squares drawn and a blue and a red piece on it. Debate has few written rules, so teams argue about the rest.
slots.caption: Debate has few written rules; theory is how teams argue about the rest.

slots.purpose: Show the four parts of a theory argument, and the two remedies the voter can ask for.
slots.diagram_spec: Four rounded boxes in one row, left to right, joined by plain arrows pointing right. Box 1: title 'Interpretation', line 'The rule that should apply'. Box 2: title 'Violation', line 'How the other team broke it'. Box 3: title 'Standards', line 'Why the rule is good for debate'. Box 4: title 'Voter', line 'What the judge should do about it'. From box 4, two short arrows branch down to two small result boxes side by side: 'Reject the argument: ignore it, decide the rest normally' and 'Reject the team: vote against the team that made it'. Under the first row, one centred line of small text: 'Same shape as topicality. The other team answers with a counter-interpretation.' Ink outlines and text, white fills, light grey #e1e4e8 behind the titles. No blue or red, because either team can run theory. On narrow screens the four boxes stack top to bottom with arrows pointing down, and the two result boxes stack under the last one.
slots.alt: Diagram of a theory argument: interpretation, violation, standards and voter in a row, with the voter splitting into reject the argument or reject the team.
slots.caption: A theory argument has the same four parts as topicality, and ends with a remedy.

slots.purpose: Conditionality lets the negative put out several options and drop some of them later in the round.
slots.subject: Three plain tent-shaped cards, like folded place cards, in a row on a flat surface. The middle card still stands upright. The left and right cards have been laid down flat on the surface.
slots.composition: Front view, slightly from above. The three cards sit in an even row across the middle of the frame, with equal gaps. The two flat cards lie in the same spots where they stood. A thin ground line runs under them. Nothing else is in the picture.
slots.colors: All three cards are white with neg red #f2232d outlines, because they are the negative's options. The surface line is light grey #e1e4e8. No blue.
slots.avoid: No hands, people, arrows, bins or crumpled paper. No writing on the cards. Do not make the flat cards look torn or thrown.
slots.alt: Three red cards in a row: one still stands, two are laid flat. Conditionality lets the neg run several options and drop some of them later.
slots.caption: Conditionality lets the negative run options and drop some later.

slots.purpose: The two main remedies differ in size: set aside one argument, or decide the round against the team.
slots.subject: Two small identical game boards side by side, each a plain square with a simple grid. On the left board, three round pieces stand on the board and one matching piece has been set just off the board's edge. On the right board, the board is empty and all four pieces stand together just off the board's edge.
slots.composition: Seen from slightly above. The two boards sit side by side across the middle of the frame, the same size, with a clear white gap between them. On each board the removed pieces sit just below the board's lower right corner. Nothing else is in the picture.
slots.colors: Boards are white with black outlines and light grey #e1e4e8 squares. All pieces are white with black outlines. No blue or red, because either team can win a theory argument.
slots.avoid: No hands, people, arrows, crosses or bins. Do not show pieces knocked over or broken.
slots.alt: Two game boards: on one, a single piece is set aside; on the other, all pieces are removed. The judge can reject the argument or reject the team.
slots.caption: Reject the argument sets one piece aside; reject the team decides the round against that team.

slots.purpose: Most common theory arguments ask which counterplan and perm routes are fair to take.
slots.subject: A main road runs across the picture. Three side paths branch off it. At the start of each side path stands a simple swing gate: a single plain bar on a post. The gates are at different positions: one fully open, one half open, one closed across its path.
slots.composition: Seen from slightly above. The main road enters at the left edge and leaves at the right edge at mid height. The three side paths branch upward from it at even spacing, left, centre and right. Each gate sits where its path leaves the road. Nothing else is in the picture.
slots.colors: Road and paths are light grey #e1e4e8 with black edges. Gates and posts are white with black outlines. No blue or red.
slots.avoid: No signs, stripes that look like writing, locks, cars, people, arrows or traffic lights. Do not use red and white barrier stripes.
slots.alt: A road with three side paths, each with a gate that is open, half open or closed. Common theory arguments ask which counterplan routes are fair.
slots.caption: Most common theory arguments ask which routes a counterplan or perm may take.

slots.purpose: Fiat lets the debate treat the plan as passed, so the round is about whether it should pass.
slots.subject: A plain sheet with four straight lines lies flat. A simple rubber stamp, with a round handle and a flat base, has just lifted off the sheet. On the lower part of the sheet is the plain solid circle it left behind.
slots.composition: Seen from slightly above. The sheet lies across the centre, a little left. The stamp hovers just above and to the right of the circle mark, tilted slightly, as if just lifted. Nothing else is in the picture.
slots.colors: The sheet and stamp are white with black outlines. The sheet's lines are ink. The stamped circle is mid grey #7d8690. No blue or red, because both teams use fiat.
slots.avoid: No words, stars, eagles, seals with patterns, government buildings, flags, hands or wands. The circle must be completely plain.
slots.alt: A stamp has just left a plain circle on a plan sheet. Fiat lets the debate imagine the plan passes, so the round is about whether it should.
slots.caption: Fiat asks the judge to imagine the plan passes.
